target_customer: Individual professionals and teams who repeatedly send the same emails, links, images and replies
problem: People retype or hunt for the same snippets, templates and links across web apps.
business_model: Chrome extension productivity tool; monetization not found

founders.name: Lambert Chu
education: MIT, computer science and management science
founders.background_notes: From the YC page, which lists him as co-founder and CTO; the other founder is not named there.

technical_complexity.rationale: A browser extension that stores and inserts snippets across sites is standard engineering, with some work to support many web apps.

defensibility.rationale: Text expanders and Gmail templates already existed and the feature is easy to copy.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Gmail has a built in templates feature, and other extensions served the need; no evidence of acquisition.

market_need_then: Repeated typing of support and sales replies is a common pain, but dated evidence of paying demand was not found.

branding.domain_note: Used pointapi.com, a suffixed domain rather than point.com.

identity.voice_and_tone: Playful copy with a shrug emoticon in the YC description.

brand_strength.rationale: A generic word shared with many other companies, including a challenger bank also called Point, and no sourced press about the brand.

outcome_analysis: Point was a Chrome extension for storing and reusing frequently sent text, links and images, backed by Y Combinator and seed investors from Slow Ventures to Graph Ventures. Crunchbase marks it closed, but no shutdown cause is public. The brand confusion factor is a tentative inference from the generic name shared with other Point companies.
notes: Seed round and investors rest on a Crunchbase listing seen in search results only (amounts and dates hidden; the page returned 403 on fetch), a single database. The pointapi.com site returned HTTP 522. A TechCrunch article about a challenger bank called Point is unrelated. No dated competitors found; TextExpander and Gmail templates appear only on undated pages.
